THE PROPOSED FIRST STEP

Get a clearer picture before you begin.

The Café Reality Check is envisioned as an introduction to the decisions behind a café: what it takes to operate, what to plan for and where to find guidance. It is designed to help you ask better questions before committing to your next step.

Understand the commitment

Explore the day-to-day realities of café ownership, the demands on your time and the shape of a business that fits your goals.

Plan with perspective

Consider startup and operating costs, premises, equipment and the importance of working capital.

Know what comes next

Get an introduction to approvals, team needs and the practical questions to discuss with experienced partners.

THE FULL LEARNING JOURNEY

From the first idea to daily operations.

The proposed full program develops each topic in more detail through lessons, practical resources and quizzes. Course structure and availability remain subject to confirmation.

01

Is a café right for you?

Consider the lifestyle, customer service, operating demands and personal commitment behind café ownership.

02

Plan the business

Explore startup and operating costs, working capital, break-even thinking and financial projections for your own concept.

03

Find the right premises

Consider location, lease questions, the customer you want to serve and the land-use requirements relevant to a site.

04

Understand compliance

Get an introduction to food premises, hygiene, building and safety requirements, and the questions to take to the relevant authorities and specialists.

05

Choose your equipment

Explore espresso machines, grinders, water filtration, refrigeration and food preparation equipment in relation to your menu and expected service.

06

Design the space

Think through atmosphere, shop fitting and the movement of customers and staff from arrival to service.

07

Build a menu

Consider coffee, breakfast and day-trade food, ingredient costs, suppliers and consistent preparation.

08

Build your team

Explore hiring, barista skills, food hygiene and the routines that support a confident team.

09

Run the operation

Look at opening and closing routines, stock, cleaning and the role an integrated point-of-sale system could play.

10

Welcome customers back

Consider local marketing, service, loyalty and the experience that helps build regular custom.

11

Plan your next step

Bring your questions together and explore what equipment, setup, training or business support may be appropriate.

LEARNING THAT GOES FURTHER

Practical resources, not just theory.

The proposed course materials include short lessons, quizzes, checklists and equipment guidance. They are intended to help you apply each topic to your own café idea.

For hands-on development, explore practical barista training and team learning with WOSC.
